full_judgment:
5. The petitioner-company contested the complaint cases by filing written statements, denying the material allegations and stating inter alia that the cases are not maintainable in law, that the respondents are not officers of the Trade Union, that the cases are barred by limitation. 

 8. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the judgment and order dated 5.7.99 passed by the Chairman, 1st Labour Court, Chittagong, in the aforementioned complaint case are bad in law as it ordered for reinstatement of the respondents in the services with back wages whom the petitioner-company decided to simply terminate from service under section 19(1) of the said Act with all monetary termination benefit without assigning any reason or blame or stigma. Therefore, the present cases are not maintainable in view of the proviso to section 25 of the said Act. He has further submitted that the Labour Court has committed an error of law in holding that the order of termination is not proper and lawful since there is no finding that the services of the respondents were terminated for any of their trade union activities nor there were any specific proof or evidence that they were ever engaged in any legal trade union activities as provided in I.R.O. at the time of their termination from service. He has further submitted that as the union took over the dispute on 25.1.99 demanding reinstatement of the terminated staffs the petition under section 25 is no longer maintainable. Lastly, grievance petitions are absolutely barred by limitation. 

 11. As to the question of maintainability of the complaint cases it appears that the occurrence i.e. termination from services against which the grievance petitions were submitted before the authority took place on 22.1.97 and the grievance petitions were submitted on 12.6.97 in all the cases except W.P. No. 2838/99 in which case the grievance petition was submitted to the authority on 6.6.97. The law as laid down under section 25(1)(a) is that the worker concerned shall bring his grievance to the notice of his employer, in writing, within fifteen days of the occurrence of the cause of such grievance. In the instant cases we find that in all the cases the grievance petitions were submitted long after the expiry of 15 days’ time limit, Employment of Labour (Standing Order) Act being a special law should he applied strictly. The limitation cannot be condoned either by the tripartite agreement or by the Labour Court. The same view has been taken in 42 DLR258, 38DLR399.
